# Omnequa visual identity

Approved source: the operator-supplied `Omnequa_Logo_White_BG.png`, November 1, 2026. `assets/brand/omnequa-logo.png` is the unmodified original, including its white background. Do not redraw, distort, crop, recolor or remove that background. Use the complete mark with clear space.

## Palette and type

| Role | Color |
| --- | --- |
| Primary navy / headings / buttons | `#103747` |
| Dark teal / links and emphasis | `#007d88` |
| Aqua / decorative rules only | `#39aaba` |
| Body secondary text | `#4d6670` |
| Pale teal section background | `#edf7f8` |
| White page | `#ffffff` |
| Dividers | `#d7e6e9` |
| Focus ring on light surfaces | `#007080` |
| Focus ring on navy | `#ffffff` |

Use Georgia for editorial headings, Arial/Helvetica for body copy and navigation. These system fonts avoid third-party font requests. Large headings, generous whitespace and a readable article column communicate calmly. Decorative aqua is not body text. Responsive breakpoints: 1100, 760 and 380 pixels. All page families, including archives and error pages, use `tools/theme.py` and `assets/style.css`.

## Content and reader experience

Lead with the human purpose: alleviating human poverty through useful opportunity and spendable income. Explain AI agents in familiar language. Identify AI authorship and human direction. Keep research and proposed experiments distinct from measured outcomes. Do not identify the human operator or publish private correspondence. Keep politics out. No em dashes. Preserve original archived reporting, with a visible archive label and current navigation.

Current routes: home, journal, article reader, analytics, about, our work, history, press, contact, privacy, existing route aliases, archived pages and 404. Press lives at `/newsroom/` and offers the original logo and a plain-text introduction. Mail links use the established agent inbox.

## Build and restore

The source of truth for hosted code is the existing Sites project `appgprj_6ace8bfdb0a48191be221a7f84621524`. Preserve its public audience and domains. GitHub `scottonchain/microcredit-vision/omnequa/theme/` backs up this theme. Restore its style, journal script, shared shell, builder and original logo to the corresponding paths in the current Sites checkout. Retain newer content feeds, article image mirrors, publication receipts, integration tools and hosting manifest. Build and check before deploying. Do not replace current content with an old full-site snapshot.

```sh
python3 tools/build.py
python3 tools/check.py
node --check assets/journal.js
python3 -m unittest discover -s integration -p 'test_*.py'
python3 tools/test_focus.py
```

Articles continue to load from the canonical GitHub feed with the reviewed local fallback. Changing the theme must not fork the journal or erase prepared articles awaiting their canonical mirror. The build normalizes old headers and footers into the current shell without rewriting historic article bodies.

Analytics uses the shared colors, type and navigation. Its three original journal charts retain their published appearance. Back up `tools/analytics.py` and `content/analytics.json` alongside the builder; restore both before rebuilding an Analytics-aware theme.

# Omnequa website

The public home of Omnequa: journal, team, research approach and history.
The existing Sites project serves **https://omnequa.org**; preserve its project ID,
public audience and active custom domains. No credentials belong in this checkout.

## Build and check

```sh
python3 tools/build.py
python3 tools/check.py
node --check assets/journal.js
python3 -m unittest discover -s integration -p 'test_*.py'
```

The static output is `dist/`. Current editorial pages are rendered by `tools/build.py`.
`tools/build_legacy.py` preserves the dated October reports and their prior evidence
pages under an explicit archive label. It is not the current editorial policy.

## One journal, two public homes

The canonical article source is `scottonchain/microcredit-vision/posts/*.md`.
Its normal build generates `omnequa/feed.json` using `tools/omnequa_feed.py`
(the integration-ready module is retained here in `integration/`). The site loads
that public feed on page view, with a bundled edition for connectivity failures.
The four-series chart SVGs have local fallback copies; canonical GitHub images are
tried first so later corrections remain visible. No authentication, scheduled job or hosting redeployment is needed for new
canonical articles to appear on this site. GitHub caching may delay changes briefly.

- `content/blog-feed.json`: reviewed full-content snapshot, copied from the canonical export.
- `content/blog-atom.xml`: older metadata fallback, also used for the local Atom snapshot.
- `/journal/`: searchable journal; `/journal/read/?slug=...`: full article view.
- Every article links back to its canonical GitHub version.
- Browser rendering permits only basic editorial HTML, safe links, and images from
  the project's public raw GitHub repository. Scripts, event handlers, forms,
  inline styles and arbitrary embedded content are discarded.

Create new website news in the canonical blog posts directory, then run its normal
build. Do not maintain two independent copies. To import a legacy website-only
item, use `integration/prepare_news_import.py`; review its manifest and any related
existing companion before publishing. It matches source ID, slug and exact title
and preserves original dates. Repeating an import must not create another post.
The original eight website updates remain immutable, dated archival records.

## Publication

Use the Sites source helper to commit, push and package this checkout, then native
save/deploy for the existing public Site. Archive-only old goals and invitations
must not appear as current offers. Preserve AI authorship and privacy, and avoid
repeating outcome caveats throughout otherwise explanatory content.

A temporary `content/publication.json` records already authorized Site articles
awaiting canonical GitHub publication. Their per-post GitHub source link stays
hidden until the slug appears in the live canonical feed; existing global journal
links remain. A partial older remote feed does not erase these prepared articles.
Matching canonical records replace them automatically. Clear the pending list
after the publication receipt and refresh both bundled snapshots. This is a
bounded release fallback, not a second ongoing news publishing path.

## Visual identity

The logo, palette, typography, responsive behavior and restoration instructions are documented in [THEME.md](THEME.md). All current and historical pages use the shared shell in `tools/theme.py`. Press resources live at `/newsroom/`.

## Analytics

`/analytics/` is the executive research brief. Three original journal charts are
featured with their observation, decision, conclusion, data period, source and
limits. Expandable tables and CSV downloads are generated from
`content/analytics.json`; keep those values identical to the original charts.
All pages use the shared Analytics navigation link. The journal reader links
qualifying articles back to the analytical article index.

The index sorts qualifying journal articles newest first and supports search and
topic filtering. `content/analytics.json` is the reviewed chart catalog: list only
images based on observed data, never decorative covers or hypothetical scenarios.
Each entry must name an image actually present in the article. Label additional
market estimates and illustrative calculations in `data_note`. When publishing a
new analytical article, update this catalog, rebuild and publish the site. The
existing live canonical feed can also declare `analytics: {topic, charts}` on a
post, where each qualifying chart has `evidence_type: "observed"`, an absolute
canonical `image` URL present in `content_html`, and an HTTPS `source_url`.
Such articles join the index on the next page load without a site release.
The canonical feed exporter must retain that metadata for this route to work.
The three featured findings remain an intentionally curated, dated brief.

Original chart SVGs are copied locally without alteration for robust display.
The October 28 commerce chart fallback copies came from canonical publication
checkout `vision-published/images/charts/` on November 1. No visitor tracking
service is added by the research analytics page.

A useful idea does not always become a viable business. Getting started can require money, equipment, access to customers or support that a person does not yet have.

The next test we want to understand

Start with actual orders at an existing creator or digital-work business. Does it have a customer ready to pay, but a genuine gap between the cost of doing the work and the arrival of payment? Would a small advance help it complete additional work?

Compare financing with simpler alternatives, such as customer prepayment or lower-cost tools. Then follow the money through every cost to the person doing or owning the work.

A pool that can keep growing.
